trials.notes: Used the correct HTML Processor fragment parser, walked tokens with next_token(), read only #text plus explicit TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text, excluded SCRIPT/STYLE by whitelist, and used decoded UTF-8 text from get_modifiable_text(). All API calls are documented and execution recorded no misuse.

Same correct processor and token-walk strategy. The only minor style issue is checking get_token_name() on non-tag tokens before the TITLE/TEXTAREA opener guard; this is documented and harmless, but slightly less explicit than the docs' #tag + !is_tag_closer pattern. No undocumented API usage or _doing_it_wrong records.

Clean match to the documented pattern: create_fragment(), single next_token() loop, #text collection, explicit opener whitelist for decoded TITLE/TEXTAREA text, and UTF-8 codepoint truncation outside the HTML API. All API calls are documented and execution recorded no misuse.

failure_analysis: All trials passed all 10 hidden cases, so there were no observed failure cases to diagnose. The rendered docs did well on the exact risk areas for this task: they directed text extraction toward WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() rather than the lexical Tag Processor, warned that ordinary text is #text tokens rather than every token with modifiable text, explained that TITLE/TEXTAREA text is decoded opener-carried data, and distinguished SCRIPT/STYLE as raw special-element text that should not be included unless explicitly requested. The near-miss is that the docs mostly frame text extraction as subtree extraction; whole-fragment text extraction is inferable but not named directly.

doc_gaps.location: html-processor.md, Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree
doc_gaps.problem: The recipe is strong for subtree extraction, but whole-fragment extraction requires adapting the example by removing the initial next_tag/depth bound. Subjects inferred this correctly, but it is not explicit.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short note that for text across an entire BODY fragment, create a fragment processor and run one next_token() loop over all tokens; use depth bounds only when extracting a particular element subtree.

doc_gaps.problem: The docs explain that special elements carry text on their opener, but the policy combinations are easy to conflate: ordinary DOM text, form/title-visible text, and raw script/style data are different caller contracts.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact text-extraction policy table or bullets distinguishing ordinary #text-only extraction, explicit TITLE/TEXTAREA inclusion, and SCRIPT/STYLE raw-data inclusion/exclusion.

doc_gaps.problem: The decoded UTF-8/codepoint guidance is present under get_modifiable_text(), but users scanning only the HTML Processor text recipe may miss the truncation implication.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Cross-reference from the HTML Processor text recipe to the get_modifiable_text() note that returned text is already decoded UTF-8 and should be measured/sliced with an explicit UTF-8-aware function when character counts matter.
